finding: The selected Canvas node resize handle was a pointer-only focusable button. Keyboard-only users had no equivalent to pointer resizing; at reduced Canvas zoom its touch target also fell below its intended CSS-pixel size.

details: The selected, effectively-unlocked, non-root Canvas node can be resized from the focused handle: left/right change width and up/down change height by 1 CSS pixel; Shift+arrow changes the matching dimension by 10 CSS pixels. Width and height clamp at 24 CSS pixels; Ctrl/Alt/Meta modified keys are left to system/browser shortcuts.

Keyboard resize uses the existing responsive.set Page Model command and undo history with a per-node/device typing group; it rerenders, restores focus to the handle, and announces the responsive size. The handle carries a node-specific accessible name, key-shortcuts, and a Hungarian description.
The handle keeps a 26 CSS-pixel visual target through Canvas zoom, with its position compensated so it remains anchored to the node corner. Root and locked nodes do not expose resize controls.

Only the active responsive draft changes. Undo/Redo and Save/reload do not publish; explicit Publish is the separate action that changes the public version. Cache tokens and the 396-item source traceability hash were refreshed.
change.third_party_code_or_dependency: NONE; native button, existing responsive.set command/history, no added package.

coverage: Existing Canvas keyboard movement remains green at mobile and desktop widths.
Resize keys, 1px/10px increments, system-modifier pass-through, focus restoration, accessible labeling, and >=24px rendered handle target at mobile/desktop.
24px size clamp, root/locked protection, Undo/Redo, draft Save and reload, explicit Publish separation, and no browser page errors.
